title: Judo Bank - General Discussion
body:
O.P.
I see they're offering upto 3.75% term deposit atm and this seems rather high compares to other banks or financial institutions.
Seems pretty good and better than the returns on some rental.
My questions are; is it a legit bank and should there be any concerns?
Thanks

---- replies ----
[User #24425316812 postsAumInner Peace -->> World PeaceWhirlpool Forums Addict] lkj2020 writes...
My questions are; is it a legit bank and should there be any concerns?
Yes, they are legit, shouldn't be any concerns, they are business focused rather than personal. That is a decent rate depending on the term, worth a look :)
[User #488763528 posts941Whirlpool Enthusiast] lkj2020 writes...
My questions are; is it a legit bank and should there be any concerns?
Ditto to Aum's reply above. I have banked with Judo previously (personal term deposits) and found their service and their support prompt and efficient.
Note that their rates often change regularly, sometimes daily, so if you decide to deposit with them do it that day.
For your peace of mind, you can confirm for yourself that Judo is an ADI and hence funds up to $250K are guaranteed : https://www.apra.gov.au/regis ter-of-authorised-deposit-taking-institutions
[User #79193913053 postsgregbluesWhirlpool Forums Addict] lkj2020 writes...
My questions are; is it a legit bank and should there be any concerns?
Nope I have several term deposits with them and will open a few more when some money comes through from another bank. I will put up to 250k with Judo as this the amount guaranteed by the government.
I suspect Judo will go the same was as some of the other Neo banks and be taken over by one of the big 4.
[User #90234169 postsEvil GeniusHacked by the Kook. STFU CrazyParticipant] Rates look fairly normal. Macquarie has higher rates for their 1 year deposits. 2.5%
It's really strange that the other big players like St George usually had some good offerings, but I remember after they got sold it went downhill.
Term deposits usually follow the yield curve, but you will find that most banks will not pass on this money and instead earn it for themselves.

Crazy Spy writes...
Term deposits usually follow the yield curve, but you will find that most banks will not pass on this money and instead earn it for themselves.
Is it not term deposit is locked to the advertised interest rate unless you breach the conditions?
[User #8985851163 postsBatmanAUWhirlpool Enthusiast] 941 writes...
For your peace of mind, you can confirm for yourself that Judo is an ADI and hence funds up to $250K are guaranteed
So what if you had $500K, should you break it up across banks if your only covered to $250K?
[User #488763528 posts941Whirlpool Enthusiast] BatmanAU writes...
So what if you had $500K, should you break it up across banks if your only covered to $250K?
If you want the government guarantee that is capped at $250K per ADI, then yes.
[User #1577114347 postsslapnutWhirlpool Forums Addict] BatmanAU writes...
So what if you had $500K
Joint accounts are covered up tp $250k per person so $500k
[User #8985851163 postsBatmanAUWhirlpool Enthusiast] Finally sent an application through to these clowns, got the email stating was successful with the transfer details, went into Commbank and did a bank transfer to Judo. Got a call a few days later from Commbank stating that their bank didnt accept the transfer. Tried contacting these idiots a few times with no success. Got an email 10 days later stating my account was closed due to no funds.
Went to Gateway bank and they matched the term rates, move it all to them, happy now.
[User #9045181 postsQuicksilver.I'm new here, please be nice] I always check the banks director’s if unsure how legit they are. I was looking at Judo until I saw that George Obeid was a director and shall now avoid his family’s corrupt business ethics. Looks like you made a good call
[User #7331391099 postsMalleysWhirlpool Enthusiast] Quicksilver. writes...
his family
I have seen nothing to indicate that he is a member of that particular family.
I have been a customer for many years. I can't say that my customer experience has been absolutely perfect and painless but their rates and especially their loyalty bonuses keep me a customer. That said, I would swap to another bank if there were better rates offered in an instant (and lately, there often are).
[User #109938269 postsDCWForum Regular] I've been having some issues with Judo Bank support (more precisely my wife is having problems).
Due to iiNet getting out of the email business, we've both got new email addresses and have had to change all accounts linked to the old addresses. With Judo, it's easy to change the contact email address, but this doesn't change the login email address (username).
We contacted them about a month ago to ask them to change it and were told it had to be done behind the scenes by their "technical support". When nothing happened after a week or two we had a long session with one of their support staff and were assured that it had been done and should work. Eventually they accepted that it wasn't working and we were told we'd be contacted when it was sorted out.
Long story short – it still isn't fixed and today we were at first told that we would have to continue to use the old email address "due to their new platform". I argued that this could lead to confusion and possible security issues in the future, and after another couple of calls was told that it had been passed to the "Digital Team" who would contact us when it was sorted. They gave no timescale and insisted that if we didn't get a call it was because they were still working on it.
Surely they must have had other customers change an email address? Once we have lost control of the old email addresses it is imperative that it isn't linked to any financial accounts for obvious reasons.
The more I see of banks and their systems the less I am surprised that there are so many security issues, hacks, scams and identity theft problems.
[User #8879722591 posts27.56Whirlpool Forums Addict] DCW writes...
addresses it is imperative that it isn't linked to any financial accounts for obvious reasons.
In what way do you foresee any problems? I can't see any extra risk in having an old email address for a user name.
[User #109938269 postsDCWForum Regular] Old email addresses are outside my control. If anyone were to gain control of the old email account (perhaps the address can be recycled for instance), it makes my bank account less secure, perhaps giving someone a bit of a leg up to access it.
Obviously this is very unlikely, and in this case presumably impossible as iiNet won't be provisioning new email addresses.
However, as a point of principle is it much better if all links with the old address were severed and not unreasonable to expect from a bank.
[User #8879722591 posts27.56Whirlpool Forums Addict] Some banks will use a client number for the user name while others use email addresses. I find the email address ones a bit easier to remember than a customer number, but I do sympathise with you in the sense that I have a feeling of less security involved. I hold old and new addresses in the same light though. I don't think email address recycling is a thing but perhaps others can weigh in on this. In any case, I don't think that would allow anyone any better chance of accessing your funds. You've updated your new address for contact purposes so that should be fine.
In these days of using banking apps, user names of any sort have been made redundant, so perhaps banks might be more likely to return to using numbers.
